profile.name: Therapy Chat Podcast
profile.description:
Therapy Chat Podcast is hosted by Laura Reagan, LCSW-C, an integrative trauma psychotherapist, Clinical Supervisor, Consultant, Coach, Speaker and Trainer. 

Laura interviews therapists, authors and other experts about psychotherapy, trauma, attachment, mindfulness, perfectionism, worthiness, self-compassion, expressive arts and creativity.

Be a fly on the wall and listen to therapists discuss trauma focused psychotherapy techniques and self-care to prevent burnout, covering mindfulness, Brainspotting, EMDR, art therapy, and other integrative and somatic methods. They explore trauma, parenting, attachment, and the human experience of joy and suffering.

All videos copyright Trauma Therapy Coaching & Consulting, LLC. All rights reserved. Please do not distribute without attribution.

pages.excerpt: Skip to contentTrauma Therapist NetworkAbout Podcasts Therapy Chat Podcast Trauma Chat Podcast Resources Blog TTN Membership Retreats For Therapists Find a Therapist Therapy Chat Podcast Since its start in August 2015, Therapy Chat has over 490 episodes, has been heard in 160+ countries, and has over 8 Million Downloads! With hundreds of episodes about trauma, mental health, therapy, and wellness, Therapy Chat is ranked among the top .05% most downloaded podcasts in every genre. Host of Therapy Chat Laura Reagan LCSW-C Overview Therapy Chat Podcast conversations focus on healing trauma and attachment wounds with mindfulness, self-compassion, EMDR, Brainspotting, parts work and other integrative and somatic psychotherapy approaches as well as energy work and indigenous healing practices. You’ll hear compassionate discussions about rebuilding self trust, recovering from betrayal trauma, identifying unhealthy family dynamics, breaking cycles of intergenerational trauma, narcissistic abuse, parental estrangement, emotional immaturity, codependency, reconnecting to intuition, developing boundaries in relationships, neuroscience, creativity, self-care, perfectionism, worthiness and much more. Host Laura Reagan, LCSW-C shares wisdom gained from her personal lived experience and more than 20 years working with trauma survivors in grassroots settings, community mental health, the military, her group psychotherapy private practice. As a therapist with developmental trauma, Laura is sensitive to the challenges of healing from abuse, neglect, and loss, and she shares from her own journey so listeners can learn that Trauma is Real, Healing is Possible and Help is Available. Whether you’re a mental health professional or not, the discussions heard on Therapy Chat will teach you to understand yourself and your relationships more deeply, and to connect with others from your highest self. You’ll learn about alternatives to traditional talk therapy. Therapy Chat focuses on “bottom-up” approaches to healing trauma. Be a fly on the wall as Laura and her guests talk about psychotherapy in ways that might surprise you! pages.title: About Counseling Directory - Trauma Therapist Network
pages.excerpt: Skip to contentTrauma Therapist NetworkAbout Podcasts Therapy Chat Podcast Trauma Chat Podcast Resources Blog TTN Membership Retreats For Therapists Find a Therapist About Counseling Directory Welcome to the Trauma Therapist Network! We hope you will find resources, information, and support with our counseling directory whether you hope to learn about trauma or you’re looking to find a trauma therapist near me (or both!). And if you’re a trauma therapist, we hope you will find this to be a supportive community to find referrals and learn about the abundance of resources available for both clinicians and non-mental health professionals. How To Use the Trauma Therapist Network Site This site is intended as a resource to learn about trauma and find help with our trauma directory. Browsing through the pages of the site you’ll find lists of resources including crisis hotlines, private and nonprofit organizations serving trauma survivors, recommended podcasts, websites, books, articles, blogs, newsletters, and more. You’ll also find a counseling directory with listings of trauma therapists that is searchable by zip code and by specialization. To find a trauma therapist in your area, just enter your zip code and the search criteria you are seeking. As more therapists join the site, more options will be available. If you’re a trauma therapist, you can give and receive support, clinical consultation, self care practices, learn about trauma related topics, network with other trauma therapists and market your therapy practice by joining the membership community. Who Is the Trauma Therapist Network Site For? Trauma affects all of us. Although we live in a world which is seemingly unaware of the long-term impact of trauma. This includes not understanding the imapact of: natural disasters famine, poverty oppression marginalization pandemics family and community violence and decades of wars The truth is those factors have led to a high incidence of unmet mental health needs in our world’s population. Initially, Trauma Therapist Network will focus on the United States, and as our capacity grows we can expand to list resources worldwide. This site is for anyone who wants to learn about trauma and find help for self or someone they care about. Click Here To Watch A Short Video About Why Trauma Therapist Network Was Created! pages.title: Supporting Partners of Trauma Survivors with Heather Tuba - Trauma Therapist Network
pages.excerpt: Skip to contentTrauma Therapist NetworkAbout Podcasts Therapy Chat Podcast Trauma Chat Podcast Resources Blog TTN Membership Retreats For Therapists Find a Therapist Episode 176Supporting Partners of Trauma Survivors with Heather TubaDate Aired: March 28, 2019 ShareFacebookTweetPin Therapy Chat Episode 176 Welcome back to Therapy Chat! In today’s episode, host Laura Reagan, LCSW-C speaks to Heather Tuba about her work supporting partners of people who are survivors of trauma. Heather offers a beautiful perspective on her important work, which is much needed since and estimated 80% of adults in the US have experienced trauma in childhood. While the public is gradually becoming more aware of trauma survivors’ needs for support, their partners are often overlooked and Heather has been working tirelessly to change that. Heather Tuba is a writer, advocate, and certified trauma recovery coach. She is the founder of Heather Tuba Trauma-Informed Partner Support, a website dedicated to partners of survivors. She is also the founder of and Partners to Survivors with Complex PTSD, the only online support group for those in intimate relationships with adults with C-PTSD. She is the author of two resource guides for partners and offers one-on-one coaching support as well as educational consults for professionals interested in learning how to better support partners. Heather’s work is a result of her personal experience as a partner. When her husband of twenty years began to experience once-dissociated memories of childhood abuse, their life was turned upside down. Not only was she left with the task of finding him help, she knew she needed support. Finding none, she began to blog about childhood trauma and in 2017, focused exclusively on partners. Her areas of expertise include partner care, specifically the impact of dissociation and dissociated parts on partner relationships, and supporting yourself while your partner is in recovery. She is a fervent advocate for partners, most of whom are in situations of overwhelm and exhaustion. Her belief is that support groups and one-on-one support can help alleviate the stress on both partners and survivors. Resources Find Heather Tuba at – www.heathertuba.com Click here for Therapy Chat episode 128 with Dr. David Treleaven, on trauma sensitive mindfulness. Here is a past episode of Therapy Chat: When Your Partner Doesn’t Unders

pages.excerpt: Skip to contentTrauma Therapist NetworkAbout Podcasts Therapy Chat Podcast Trauma Chat Podcast Resources Blog TTN Membership Retreats For Therapists Find a Therapist Resources for Trauma, PTSD, and Complex PTSDShareFacebookTweetPin Updated: 8/1/2021 If you have experienced an event which interfered with your capacity to cope at the time, it is very likely that this experience could still be affecting you, even years later. The good news is that healing is always possible! Just as our brains are shaped/changed by negative experiences that we may have endured, our brains are also shaped/changed by positive experiences. Thank goodness for neuroplasticity! The following resources are for anyone who wants to understand whether they have been through trauma, wants to learn more about trauma, or needs assistance with finding resources which can assist on their journey to healing from trauma. This is not a comprehensive list of resources for trauma, PTSD and C-PTSD. This list is continuously updated. If you would like to submit a suggestion to be added to the list, please use our contact form on the home page. Resources for Trauma National Center on Domestic Violence, Trauma & Mental Health: This website has a lot of useful information on domestic violence and trauma for advocates and survivors. SAMHSA: SAMHSA’s programs and campaigns offer information, training, and technical assistance to improve the quality and delivery of behavioral health services across the nation. Sidran Institute: Home: Provides information about trauma, a glossary, and two different types of trainings. The National Child Traumatic Stress Network This website contains a lot of informational resources on child trauma. Resources for PTSD Mobile Apps – PTSD: National Center for PTSD: This link will give you access to a bunch of different PTSD-related applications including, PTSD Coach, PTSD Family Coach, Beyond MST, Mindfulness Coach, and more. National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health: This website is helpful for those who need help understanding complex scientific topics that relate to health research. New Online Course Helps People Who May Have Posttraumatic Stress Disorder: The National Alliance on Mental Illness created this course to help those who either think they have PTSD, or have been diagnosed with PTSD. You’ll hear compassionate discussions about rebuilding self trust, recovering from betrayal trauma, identifying unhealthy family dynamics, breaking cycles of intergenerational trauma, narcissistic abuse, parental estrangement, emotional immaturity, codependency, reconnecting to intuition, developing boundaries in relationships, neuroscience, creativity, self-care, perfectionism, worthiness and much more. Host Laura Reagan, LCSW-C shares wisdom gained from her personal lived experience and more than 20 years working with trauma survivors in grassroots settings, community mental health, the military, her group psychotherapy private practice. As a therapist with developmental trauma, Laura is sensitive to the challenges of healing from abuse, neglect, and loss, and she shares from her own journey so listeners can learn that Trauma is Real, Healing is Possible and Help is Available. You’ll learn about alternatives to traditional talk therapy. Therapy Chat focuses on “bottom-up” approaches to healing trauma. Be a fly on the wall as Laura and her guests talk about psychotherapy in ways that might surprise you! pages.excerpt: Skip to contentTrauma Therapist NetworkAbout Podcasts Therapy Chat Podcast Trauma Chat Podcast Resources Blog TTN Membership Retreats For Therapists Find a Therapist About Counseling Directory Welcome to the Trauma Therapist Network! We hope you will find resources, information, and support with our counseling directory whether you hope to learn about trauma or you’re looking to find a trauma therapist near me (or both!). And if you’re a trauma therapist, we hope you will find this to be a supportive community to find referrals and learn about the abundance of resources available for both clinicians and non-mental health professionals. How To Use the Trauma Therapist Network Site This site is intended as a resource to learn about trauma and find help with our trauma directory. Browsing through the pages of the site you’ll find lists of resources including crisis hotlines, private and nonprofit organizations serving trauma survivors, recommended podcasts, websites, books, articles, blogs, newsletters, and more. You’ll also find a counseling directory with listings of trauma therapists that is searchable by zip code and by specialization. To find a trauma therapist in your area, just enter your zip code and the search criteria you are seeking. As more therapists join the site, more options will be available. If you’re a trauma therapist, you can give and receive support, clinical consultation, self care practices, learn about trauma related topics, network with other trauma therapists and market your therapy practice by joining the membership community. Who Is the Trauma Therapist Network Site For? Trauma affects all of us. Although we live in a world which is seemingly unaware of the long-term impact of trauma. This includes not understanding the imapact of: natural disasters famine, poverty oppression marginalization pandemics family and community violence and decades of wars The truth is those factors have led to a high incidence of unmet mental health needs in our world’s population. Initially, Trauma Therapist Network will focus on the United States, and as our capacity grows we can expand to list resources worldwide. This site is for anyone who wants to learn about trauma and find help for self or someone they care about. Click Here To Watch A Short Video About Why Trauma Therapist Network Was Created! pages.title: Supporting Partners of Trauma Survivors with Heather Tuba - Trauma Therapist Network
pages.excerpt: Skip to contentTrauma Therapist NetworkAbout Podcasts Therapy Chat Podcast Trauma Chat Podcast Resources Blog TTN Membership Retreats For Therapists Find a Therapist Episode 176Supporting Partners of Trauma Survivors with Heather TubaDate Aired: March 28, 2019 ShareFacebookTweetPin Therapy Chat Episode 176 Welcome back to Therapy Chat! In today’s episode, host Laura Reagan, LCSW-C speaks to Heather Tuba about her work supporting partners of people who are survivors of trauma. Heather offers a beautiful perspective on her important work, which is much needed since and estimated 80% of adults in the US have experienced trauma in childhood. While the public is gradually becoming more aware of trauma survivors’ needs for support, their partners are often overlooked and Heather has been working tirelessly to change that. Heather Tuba is a writer, advocate, and certified trauma recovery coach. She is the founder of Heather Tuba Trauma-Informed Partner Support, a website dedicated to partners of survivors. She is also the founder of and Partners to Survivors with Complex PTSD, the only online support group for those in intimate relationships with adults with C-PTSD. She is the author of two resource guides for partners and offers one-on-one coaching support as well as educational consults for professionals interested in learning how to better support partners. Heather’s work is a result of her personal experience as a partner. When her husband of twenty years began to experience once-dissociated memories of childhood abuse, their life was turned upside down. Not only was she left with the task of finding him help, she knew she needed support. Finding none, she began to blog about childhood trauma and in 2017, focused exclusively on partners. Her areas of expertise include partner care, specifically the impact of dissociation and dissociated parts on partner relationships, and supporting yourself while your partner is in recovery. She is a fervent advocate for partners, most of whom are in situations of overwhelm and exhaustion. Her belief is that support groups and one-on-one support can help alleviate the stress on both partners and survivors.
